issues.legal_issue: A claimant does not acquire a binding joint-tenancy right through a declaration based on a limited tenant’s purported grant when the statutory conditions for co-tenancy are absent and the reversioners are not bound by the decree.
material_facts: The deceased tenant’s widow inherited only a life interest in the tenancy under the applicable tenancy law.
A third party claimed joint-tenancy rights through a declaration decree obtained in proceedings brought while the widow held that limited interest.
There was no written recognition of the claimed co-tenancy by the landholder, and the claimant was not a co-tenant from the start of the tenancy or by succession.
The reversioners were not made parties to the declaration proceedings, and the consolidation authorities found the decree collusive and fraudulent.
The widow did not ratify the claimed joint tenancy after later acquiring full ownership.
issues.conclusion: The claimant acquired no joint-tenancy right binding on the reversioners; the declaration decree did not establish such a right.
issues.legal_principle: Section 33(2) and its proviso of the U.P. Tenancy Act, 1939 require co-tenancy to exist from the commencement of the tenancy, arise by succession, or be specifically recognised in writing by the landholder; sharing cultivation alone is insufficient. Sections 35–37 address succession and the limited nature of a widow’s interest. Section 59 permits a declaration of tenant or joint-tenant status only where the requisite pre-existing co-tenancy right exists. A person claiming through a limited tenant must join the reversioners if the decree is to bind them; an encumbrance by the limited holder without them does not bind their interests.

rule.if: declaratory_tenancy_claim and inherited_life_tenancy and written_recognition_absent and cotenancy_not_from_inception_or_succession and (reversioners_not_joined or decree_collusive_or_fraudulent) and later_ratification_absent

predicates.declaratory_tenancy_claim: A claimant sought recognition of a tenancy or joint-tenancy right through a declaration proceeding.
predicates.inherited_life_tenancy: A person inherited only a life interest in the tenancy from the deceased tenant.
predicates.written_recognition_absent: The landholder did not specifically recognise the claimed co-tenancy in writing.
predicates.cotenancy_not_from_inception_or_successi: The claimant was neither a co-tenant from the tenancy’s commencement nor a successor to a co-tenant.
predicates.reversioners_not_joined: The persons entitled to the estate after the limited holder were not parties to the declaration proceeding.
predicates.decree_collusive_or_fraudulent: The decree relied on to establish the claimed right was found to be collusive or fraudulent.
predicates.later_ratification_absent: The limited holder did not ratify the claimed co-tenancy after acquiring full ownership.

issues.definition: When a declaration claim rests on a limited tenant’s interest, the claimant lacks the required origin or recognition of co-tenancy, the reversioners are unbound or the decree is tainted, and there is no later ratification, the claimant acquires no joint-tenancy right binding on the reversioners.

issues.legal_issue: A temporary statutory protection against eviction does not itself give a cultivating tenant or a limited-interest successor an alienable ownership interest before the later statutory vesting of full ownership.
material_facts: The widow succeeded to her husband’s tenancy as a limited holder.
She obtained a declaration under a temporary statute that protected her against eviction by the landholder.
No instrument transferring or encumbering the land was executed under that temporary protection.
The later land-reform vesting made the widow a full owner of the holding.
issues.conclusion: The temporary protection gave the widow a right not to be evicted, not an earlier right to alienate or encumber the holding; she acquired full ownership only upon the later statutory vesting.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 5, 6 and 7(c) of the U.P. Agricultural Tenants Acquisition of Privileges Act, 1949, read with the Act’s protective purpose, provided protection against eviction pending the land-reform legislation and did not enlarge a limited interest into alienable ownership. Under the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1951, the widow acquired full ownership upon vesting. Ramji Dixit v. Bhrigunath and others, [1966] 2 SCR 767, held that a female heir who inherited a limited tenancy interest acquired absolute rights under the land-reform legislation upon vesting.

rule.if: tenancy_status_claim and inherited_limited_tenancy and temporary_protection_only_prevented_ejection and no_transfer_instrument and statutory_vesting_occurred

predicates.tenancy_status_claim: A person claimed rights in land held under a tenancy.
predicates.inherited_limited_tenancy: A successor inherited a limited tenancy interest from a deceased tenant.
predicates.temporary_protection_only_prevented_ejec: A temporary statutory declaration protected the holder from eviction without granting a transfer of ownership.
predicates.no_transfer_instrument: No instrument transferring or encumbering the holding was executed.
predicates.statutory_vesting_occurred: A later land-reform law vested full ownership of the holding in the limited holder.

issues.definition: When a successor has only a limited tenancy interest, temporary protection merely prevents eviction, no transfer instrument exists, and later statutory vesting occurs, full ownership arises only at that vesting.

issues.legal_issue: A civil court may hear a suit seeking a declaration that a tenancy decree was obtained by fraud when the revenue forum cannot grant that relief.
material_facts: The civil suit sought a declaration that a decree obtained in tenancy proceedings was fraudulent and collusive.
The revenue courts could not grant the relief sought in that civil suit.
issues.legal_principle: Section 242 of the U.P. Tenancy Act, 1939 excludes civil-court jurisdiction over rights and claims arising under that Act, but does not bar a suit for relief that revenue courts cannot provide. Section 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure preserves civil-court jurisdiction unless it is expressly or impliedly excluded.

predicates.civil_suit_seeks_fraud_declaration: A plaintiff brought a civil suit seeking to set aside or discredit a decree on the ground of fraud or collusion.
predicates.revenue_forum_cannot_grant_that_relief: The revenue forum lacked power to grant the relief sought in the civil suit.

issues.definition: When a civil suit seeks a fraud-based declaration that the revenue forum cannot grant, the civil court has jurisdiction.

issues.legal_issue: After a consolidation notification ousts civil-court jurisdiction and abates a pending suit, consolidation authorities may consider evidence and findings already recorded in that suit unless contrary evidence is established.
material_facts: A civil proceeding concerning the land was pending when a consolidation notification was published.
The proceeding abated and the consolidation authorities acquired exclusive jurisdiction to decide the dispute.
The consolidation authorities considered evidence and findings from the civil suit and appeal, although no fresh evidence was adduced before them.
No contrary evidence was established to displace that material.
issues.conclusion: The abatement did not erase the evidence or findings already recorded; the consolidation authorities were entitled to consider and rely on them in the absence of contrary evidence.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 5 of the U.P. Consolidation of Holdings Act, 1953, publication of a consolidation notification transfers the dispute to the consolidation authorities and causes the pending civil proceeding to abate. Ram Adhar Singh v. Ramroop Singh and others establishes the transfer of jurisdiction. Evidence recorded and findings made before abatement are not thereby wiped out and may be considered as relevant evidence unless contradicted by other evidence.

rule.if: land_dispute_pending_in_civil_proceeding and consolidation_notification_displaces_civil_jurisdiction and prior_evidence_or_findings_exist and no_contrary_evidence_established

predicates.land_dispute_pending_in_civil_proceeding: A civil proceeding concerning a land dispute was pending when consolidation began.
predicates.consolidation_notification_displaces_civ: A consolidation notification transferred adjudication of the dispute away from the civil court and the civil proceeding abated.
predicates.prior_evidence_or_findings_exist: Evidence or findings concerning the dispute had already been recorded in the civil proceeding.
predicates.no_contrary_evidence_established: No evidence was established that contradicted the prior record.

issues.definition: When a land dispute passes from a pending civil proceeding to consolidation, prior recorded evidence or findings remain available for consideration if no contrary evidence is established.
